$comment: handle-words.json: the words of generated player handles in the scrapyard game (yard-design.md 7.6: adjective, noun, place: 'Steady Anvil of Oakbridge'). Nothing a player types is ever shown to another; these lists are all a handle can be made of. Second pass of the names step, 2026-11-25. An engineer's check, not legal or moderation clearance.

check.script: python3 scripts/content/yard/check-words.py [--wikidata]: composes every adjective + noun, noun + 'of' + place and adjective + 'of' + place (2400 + 1800 + 1200 pairs) and runs the filter of name-filter.json, the fourth game's lint lists and the four earlier games' proper names; with --wikidata it looks up every adjective + noun as an English Wikipedia title in two spellings ('Steady Anvil', 'Steadyanvil'). Result on 2026-11-25: 0 flags.
check.placesFrom: the register's places (Oakbridge, Westholm, Bellmarch, Saltreach, Flint Ridge, Eastmere, Sandport, Crane Point, Clay Coast, Cinder Lane), districts that rival firms are named after (Brookmill, Millbeck, Stonebeck, Larkmoor, Tarnmoor, Kolbeck, Gannetby, Aldermoss, Tenterby, Garrowfield, Rowkirk) and new districts (Elmbeck, Hollybeck, Highbeck, Kilnbrook, Rookmoor, Birchmoor, Alderbeck, Moorbridge, Hazelbeck). Each new district: corpus.py (four games) clear, App Store and Google Play search (US) no app, Companies House only small firms of the word (e.g. HAZELBECK none, KILNBROOK LIMITED, MOORBRIDGE FINANCIAL SERVICES), no Wikipedia page or Wikidata item of the name found for the register's places; NOT web-searched (the run's web search budget was spent).
check.removedBeforeComposing: Swift (a famous singer's surname, deny-people), Sturdy ('turd' inside), Quick, Tidy and Busy (distinctive words of names in the earlier games), Winch, Finch, Bolt (one letter from a distinctive name word: Pinch, Belt), Sharp and Smart (electronics and car brands), Thrifty (a car-hire brand), and by rule every innuendo, size, colour, metal and purity word (name-filter.json)
check.removedByPairs: Rugged (Rugged Bear, a film; Rugged Lark, a horse), Bison (Brave Bison, a media company), Spring (Early Spring, Warm Spring, a film), Oak as a noun (Fair Oak, a village; Mighty Oak, a film), Lynx (Lucky Lynx, a character), Fox (Hardy Fox, a musician; Spry Fox, a game studio), Sparrow (Mighty Sparrow, a musician), Kestrel and Rowan (letters of a slur or a rude word where the parts meet: SteadyKestrel, RowanKolbeck), Pelican (rude letters with two places, before the rule was limited to pairs written without a gap)
